item.question: A snail is trying to climb along the wall of a deep well. During the day it climbs up u cm and during the night it slowly slips down d cm. This happens for 10 days and 10 nights. (a) Write an expression describing how far away the snail is from its starting position. (b) What can we say about the snail's movement if d > u?
steps_tex: $(a)$: In one day and night the snail moves $u - d\text{ cm}$.
For $10$ days and $10$ nights the distance is $10 \times (u - d) = 10(u - d)$ centimetres.
$(b)$: If $d > u$, then $u - d$ is negative, so every day and night ends lower than it began.
The snail slips down more than it climbs, so it never reaches the top.
item.answer_tex: $(a)$: $10(u - d)$ centimetres; $(b)$: it slips down more than it climbs, so it never reaches the top

steps_tex: Week $1$: $5\text{ km}$ a day for $7$ days is $5 \times 7 = 35\text{ km}$.
Week $2$: the daily distance is $5 + z$, so $(5 + z) \times 7 = 35 + 7z\text{ km}$.
Week $3$: the daily distance is $5 + 2z$, so $(5 + 2z) \times 7 = 35 + 14z\text{ km}$.

Week 2: the daily distance is 5 + z, so (5 + z) × 7 = 35 + 7z km.
Week 3: the daily distance is 5 + 2z, so (5 + 2z) × 7 = 35 + 14z km.
item.text:
$1$. Week $1$: $5\text{ km}$ a day for $7$ days is $5 \times 7 = 35\text{ km}$.
$2$. Week $2$: the daily distance is $5 + z$, so $(5 + z) \times 7 = 35 + 7z\text{ km}$.
$3$. Week $3$: the daily distance is $5 + 2z$, so $(5 + 2z) \times 7 = 35 + 14z\text{ km}$.
$4$. Total $= 35 + (35 + 7z) + (35 + 14z) = 105 + 21z\text{ km}$.
Answer: $105 + 21z\text{ km}$

The time taken in minutes to travel from one station to the next station is the same and is denoted by t. The train stops for 2 minutes at each of the three stations. (a) If t = 4, what is the time taken to travel from Yahapur to Vahapur? (b) What is the algebraic expression for the time taken to travel from Yahapur to Vahapur? [Hint: Draw a rough diagram to visualise the situation]
steps_tex: Three stations in between make four equal journeys: Yahapur to station $1$, $1$ to $2$, $2$ to $3$, $3$ to Vahapur.
Travel time is $4 \times t$, and the stops are $3 \times 2 = 6$ minutes.
$(a)$: With $t = 4$: $4 \times 4 + 6 = 16 + 6 = 22$ minutes.
$(b)$: The expression is $4t + 6$ minutes.

steps_tex: With no fold, one cut gives $2$ pieces. One fold and a cut gives $3$ pieces.
Each extra fold adds one more piece, so the pieces are the number of folds plus $2$.

steps_tex: The cycle has $4$ positions: red at $1$, yellow at $2$, green at $3$, yellow at $4$, then it repeats.
Divide each position by $4$. Remainder $2$ or $0$ means yellow, remainder $1$ means red, remainder $3$ means green.
$90 \div 4$ leaves remainder $2$, so yellow. $190 \div 4$ leaves remainder $2$, so yellow. $343 \div 4$ leaves remainder $3$, so green.
Red is at $4n - 3$, yellow is at $2n$ (every even position), green is at $4n - 1$.

item.question: Observe the pattern of squares that grows with each step: Step 1 has 5 squares, and each step adds 4 squares. How many squares will be there in Step 4, Step 10, Step 50? Write a general formula. How would the formula change if we want to count the number of vertices of all the squares?
steps_tex: Step $1$ has $5$ squares and each step adds $4$, so Step $n$ has $5 + (n - 1) \times 4$ squares.
Simplify: $5 + 4n - 4 = 4n + 1$.
Each square has $4$ vertices, so vertices $= 4 \times (4n + 1) = 16n + 4$.
item.answer_tex: $17$, $41$ and $201$ squares; the formula is $4n + 1$; vertices $16n + 4$

item.question: Numbers are written in a particular sequence in this endless 4-column grid: row 1 holds 1, 2, 3, 4; row 2 holds 5, 6, 7, 8; and so on. (a) Give expressions to generate all the numbers in a given column (column 1, 2, 3 or 4). (b) In which row and column will the following numbers appear: (i) 124 (ii) 147 (iii) 201 (c) What number appears in row r and column c? (d) Observe the positions of multiples of 3. Do you see any pattern in it? List other patterns that you see.
steps_tex: $(a)$: Row $r$ starts after $r - 1$ full rows of $4$ numbers. Column $1$: $4(r - 1) + 1$, column $2$: $4(r - 1) + 2$, column $3$: $4(r - 1) + 3$, column $4$: $4(r - 1) + 4$.

$(b)$: $124 \div 4$ leaves remainder $0$, so $124 = 4 \times 30 + 4$, giving $r - 1 = 30$ and $c = 4$: row $31$, column $4$. $147 = 4 \times 36 + 3$: row $37$, column $3$. $201 = 4 \times 50 + 1$: row $51$, column $1$.
$(c)$: The number in row $r$ and column $c$ is $4(r - 1) + c$.
$(d)$: Multiples of $3$ fall in the columns $3$, $2$, $1$, $4$, then repeat $3$, $2$, $1$, $4$.
Other patterns: every number in column $4$ is a multiple of $4$; even numbers appear only in columns $2$ and $4$; odd numbers appear only in columns $1$ and $3$.
